newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks end lower as new data fuel Fed worries.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks end lower as new data fuel Fed worries.

text.p: U.S. blue chips suffered sharp losses for a second straight day as mounting evidence of a booming economy intensified Wall Street's fears of a near-term credit tightening by the Federal Reserve Board.
The Dow industrials fell 33 points to about 5614 in a sell-off sparked by strong July factory orders and a stunning jump in the August Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (CPMI).
"The Chicago PMI number today was very ugly," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "That seemed to be the catalyst."

The Chicago index, which jumped to an almost unheard of 60.0 from 51.2 in July, sparked a nearly full-point fall in the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond, sending the yield to 7.12 percent, nearly a seven-week high.

The index, when coupled with Thursday's hefty upward revision to gross domestic product and surging home sales data, shook markets that had largely dismissed the possibility of a rate move before the November elections.
"Until these last reports, almost no one thought the evidence would be that overwhelming," said Robert Stovall, president of Stovall/21st Advisors.

The Dow's decline Friday brought its losses for the week to roughly 109 points, its worst week-long performance since the last week of May when it dropped nearly 120 points, days after registering an all-time high close of 5778 on May 22.

The session was also among the NYSE's slowest of the year in terms of volume, which may have exaggerated the impact of the sell-off. Analysts said that while volumes may recover after Labor Day, market jitters are likely to persist.
"Next week should be a much better test for volume, but the market is still one day bullish and one day bearish," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio manager at Smith Barney.
Until recently, state regulations in Missouri prohibited outside buyers from acquiring in-state banks like Boatmen's.

The $9.5 billion proposed deal with NationsBank sparked a flurry of interest in other Missouri-based regional banks, among them Mercantile Bancorp, which rose 1-5/8 to 48-7/8 and Commerce Bancshares, up 1-1/8 to 36-1/2.

ValuJet Inc jumped 1-1/2 to 12-1/2 after winning tentative approval from the Federal Aviation Administration to resume operations. Company officials said the low-cost carrier could be flying again in a week.
